groups.title: About This Book
lines: Practical Business Japanese has been designed for people who have mastered basic Japanese, especially those people who want to polish up their Japanese for business purposes.

groups.title: Features of this book
lines: 1. This book uses the ordinary Japanese actually used in conversations at the office, and is designed to bring the non-native speaker to the level of communication necessary for doing business in Japan.

2. This book is divided into ten chapters, each with its own particular focus and set of practical expressions. The student is able to move about freely in the book, going to the sections which are particularly necessary for his or her circumstances.

3. Each unit begins with a basic conversation, includes strategic expressions, and ends with practical conversations. The basic conversation presents the objective of the unit, and the strategic expression section allows the student to learn many expressions for instant use in the office.
4. In the strategic expression section, expressions that should not be used when speaking to superiors, expressions used mainly by men, and expressions used mainly by women are also included.
5. The position of the characters is shown in order to make clear their subordinate/superior and inner group/outer group relationships.
6. The Coffee Break sections explain facets of Japanese society that foreigners might find difficult to understand.
7. Chapter 2 covers telephone conversation and includes an easy-to-understand flowchart.

groups.title: Effective use of this book
lines: 1. This book may be used as the main text in the classroom, as a supplementary text, or even as a self-study text.
2. This book should be studied not only in the classroom, but also anywhere the opportunity is presented, such as when commuting to work.

groups.title: Effective use of this book (continued)
lines: 3. Since many practical expressions are included in this book, it can also be used as a dictionary, and it probably would be a good idea to keep a copy in the office.

4. The most important thing to do is to actually try out the expressions in real life. This will help one's conversational ability and communication skills to improve, and it might even allow one to discover his or her own business opportunities.

groups.title: Features of each chapter
lines: Chapter 1 - Greetings: Various types of greetings, introductions, farewells, and comments regarding the weather are divided according to their functions.
Chapter 2 - Telephone conversation: The book introduces many situations for telephone conversation and organizes useful expressions into a quick-reference flowchart.
Chapters 3-7 - Making a request, Placing orders, Inviting, Permission, Advice: Strategic expressions and practical conversations help the student acquire living Japanese used in business.
Chapters 8-10 - Communicating information, Expressing opinions, Exchanging opinions: These chapters present the material in conversational form so that it may be acquired quickly and correctly.
The book leads the student in an orderly, easy-to-understand fashion while introducing many expressions actually used in the Japanese business world.
